key_insight: High overall decision accuracy concealed failures to escalate incompatible radiotherapy goals, while some submitted plans missed achievable hard goals.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating when AI planning agents submit, stop, or request review may reveal safety-relevant failures that dose metrics alone miss.
method: Built OpenGray with provably incompatible dose goals and feasible controls backed by stored plans.
Evaluated four planning systems on 30 head-and-neck patients, using commercial and local LLMs.
Examined decisions, dose, problem recognition, and technical failures, plus logs from 39 SAGE radiosurgery runs.
evidence_signal: With Terra, two LLM-based systems achieved 95.4% and 92.1% decision accuracy but escalated only 50% and 25% of overlap contradictions; 24% of submitted feasible-control plans missed a hard goal.
watch_item: The small evaluation does not establish clinical safety; recognizing an unsatisfied goal also requires an explicit stop-and-review action.
paper_title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents
